subject: Chain-of-Custody & Retention Carveout — CAIQ/SIG artifacts needed for tenant forensic hold
messages:
From: Maya Singh <m.singh@sterran.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, audit@sterran.com
Cc: procurements@sterran.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Evidence request — tenant-specific retention carveout and chain-of-custody artifacts

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SOC2 uplift and a pending legal hold for one of our research tenants, our security team needs a concise package that demonstrates:

- The exact retention carveout you applied to the tenant (policy snippet + config ID)
- Chain-of-custody for preserved logs and snapshots covering the window 2026-04-01 -> 2026-05-15
- CAIQ / SIG control mappings used to justify the carveout (control IDs and where artifacts live)
- Proof of deletion for logs outside the carveout window (delete timestamps, manifest)

We attached our one-page evidence checklist (sterran_evidence_req.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide:

1) A CSV manifest with object keys/timestamps for preserved objects (including checksums).
2) Kernel-level or S3 lifecycle records demonstrating deletion for out-of-scope data.
3) An exported CAIQ mapping file that shows which controls we can mark as satisfied by the carveout.

Timing: our compliance window is tight — would you be able to provide an initial deliverable by EOD 2026-06-15? If not, please propose a concrete timeline and owner.

Appreciate it — Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Security, Sterran Therapeutics

--- attachment: sterran_evidence_req.pdf (1 page, checklist)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@sterran.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 02:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Evidence request — tenant-specific retention carveout and chain-of-custody artifacts

Maya — thanks for the checklist and for outlining the window. Short answer: yes, we can provide the artifacts you described. Proposed plan below (will follow up with files):

Summary deliverables (initial package by 2026-06-15):
- redwood_chain_of_custody_manifest.csv: object key, tenant_id, capture_timestamp, checksum, retention_flag, operator_id
- redwood_log-retention-proof-stub.txt: lifecycle / delete timestamps for objects outside the carveout window + S3 object version IDs
- CAIQ_mapping_v1.xlsx: mapping of Sterran’s carveout to CAIQ control IDs and SIG questions we consider satisfied by the carveout

Owners & asks:
- Ben Carter (CC) will assemble the manifest and deletion evidence (S3/Blob metadata + lifecycle rules).
- Marissa Cole will export the CAIQ/SIG mapping and annotate which evidence artifacts map to each control.
- Irene Choi from our security team will validate chain-of-custody wording and sign off on the manifest.

Two clarifying Qs for your team:
1) Do you need KMS key rotation logs or just object-level timestamps and checksums?
2) Do you require notarized signatures or is security-team attestation sufficient for the CAIQ mapping?

If EOD 6/15 is too tight for anything, call out which item you prefer first and we’ll prioritize.

Action: I’ll ask Ben to send a proof-of-delete stub and the manifest by Friday morning (our side).

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jonas — forwarding the thread: attached are the initial artifacts we can hand off. Notes inline.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_chain_of_custody_manifest.csv (CSV, 3.2MB) — columns: object_key, tenant_id, first_capture, last_modified, checksum_sha256, retention_tag, operator_login
- redwood_log-retention-proof-stub.txt (TXT, 45KB) — formatted export of lifecycle events and object deletions (object version ids redacted in this stub)
- CAIQ_mapping_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB) — mapping doc linking carveout artifacts to CAIQ sections and SIG questions

Implementation notes:
- For deletions, we can provide S3 lifecycle delete markers + bucket access logs to show when deletion occurred. Where requested, we can also include KMS audit entries (requires security sign-off).
- Chain-of-custody: we include operator_login and a signed manifest hash (we will provide the SHA256 of the CSV as a separate artifact).
- We redacted a small set of internal debug keys from the manifest; if Sterran needs full object keys for legal forensics, we’ll need a completed NDA addendum (procurement@sterran.com is CC’d in the original request).

Timeline:
- Deliver initial package (CSV + txt + CAIQ mapping) by 2026-06-15 16:00 UTC.
- Security validation (Irene) to sign the chain-of-custody attestation by 2026-06-17.

Marissa — once Irene signs off, can you export the CAIQ with those control states and send the DocuSign link Maya requested?

Ben
Ben Carter
Security & Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks good. We received the CSV stub and the retention-proof text (redacted keys are fine for now). A few follow-ups before we close the ticket:

- KMS logs: For completeness our legal team prefers KMS key-use entries for the deletion events. Can Redwood include the KMS audit entries (you mentioned security sign-off required)?
- Manifest checksum: please provide the SHA256 of the final CSV as a separate signed artifact (can be a small text file or DocuSign attestation).
- DocuSign: please generate the CAIQ mapping DocuSign envelope that confirms which controls are satisfied by the carveout (we need an executed copy for our audit report).

Timing: if you can provide the KMS entries and signed checksum by 2026-06-17 EOD UTC that will work for us. Procurement will review the NDA addendum if full object keys are required.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Maya
